content.tl_dr: Peter Steinberger 回顾了 OpenClaw 作为增长最快开源项目的爆发式发展，以及他加入 OpenAI 负责智能体开发、同时通过 OpenClaw Foundation 保持项目独立的安排。

prerequisites: 了解大语言模型的基本概念
熟悉 GitHub 开源协作方式
了解 CVE 与 CVSS 安全术语
related_topics: 本地 LLM 与云端 API
AI 安全与提示词注入

content.overview: 在这场主题演讲和随后的问答中，Peter Steinberger 回顾了 OpenClaw 诞生后的前五个月，并称其为 GitHub 历史上增长最快的软件项目。他用“脱衣舞钢管式增长”形容这种速度：项目已接近 3 万次提交，贡献者约 2,000 人。他也回应了外界对安全问题的高度关注：OpenClaw 每天要处理 16 条以上严重安全报告，约为 Linux 内核的两倍；但他认为其中许多是研究者绕过默认安全设置后制造的失真结论或 AI 垃圾。即使本人加入 OpenAI，他仍希望通过 OpenClaw Foundation 建立类似“瑞士”的中立机制。整场讨论进一步谈到智能体软件的核心壁垒：当 AI 生成代码越来越普遍，人类的品味和系统设计比代码产量更重要。Steinberger 最终描绘了一个以本地数据所有权为基础、具备独特人格或“灵魂”、可在不同设备与空间中持续陪伴用户的智能体未来。

items.content: 项目规模：五个月内约 3 万次提交、近 3 万个 PR、约 2,000 名贡献者。
安全数据：累计 1,142 份报告，已公开 469 份，关闭率约 60%；即使边缘场景也经常被标为 CVSS 10.0。
依赖风险：未固定 Axios 版本曾让 MS Teams 或 Slack 链路暴露于供应链攻击。

sections.title: 项目指标与安全数据
sections.description: OpenClaw 的关键项目规模和安全报告数据。

items.content: 大型基金会像处于“困难模式”的公司，因为维护者不能直接命令志愿贡献者。
智能体应遵循基于长期声誉建立信任的机制，让可信实体逐步获得更高权限。
软件开发应避免全自动“黑灯工厂”；通往目标的路径从来不是直线，因此由人主导的迭代方式更可靠。

sections.title: “困难模式”下管理开源项目
sections.description: 高速度社区项目与 AI 驱动开发的管理经验。

items.content: AI 让复杂的多步攻击链更容易被发现，正在从根本上改变安全环境，并暴露大量未考虑智能体攻击者的旧软件。
智能体的“灵魂”——人格和细微习惯——不只是审美，而是在消息应用等非搜索场景中建立信任和自然互动的条件。
开源智能体框架会从个人使用向企业渗透：员工先在家中采用，再自下而上推动工作场景的 AI 使用。

sections.title: 关于 AI 智能体的更高层观察
sections.description: 对智能体软件现状和行业动力的综合判断。

keypoints.title: 超高速增长与“钢管式”轨迹
keypoints.detail: OpenClaw 被称为 GitHub 历史上增长最快的项目，已超过教育类仓库，成为平台上规模最大的功能型软件项目。五个月内约有 3 万次提交和近 3 万个 PR，这种速度迫使项目从个人维护转向由 Nvidia、Microsoft、ByteDance 等参与的广泛协作。
keypoints.evidence: I think it's fair to say by now that we are the fastest growing project in GitHub's history... a friend called it stripper pole gross and that comes with its own challenges.
keypoints.why_it_matters: 这种规模证明了市场对开放式智能体框架的强烈需求，用户希望摆脱企业数据孤岛。

keypoints.title: 安全报告洪流
keypoints.detail: 项目已收到 1,142 份安全报告，平均每天 16.6 份。Steinberger 将其与 Linux 内核每天 8 至 9 份、Curl 累计约 600 份作对比；其中 99% 被标为严重，团队不得不应对 AI 自动生成漏洞报告的新现实。
keypoints.evidence: So far we got 1,142 advisories. That's around 16.6 a day. 99% are critical... we get like twice as much as the Linux kernel.
keypoints.why_it_matters: AI 工具能够发现复杂的多步利用链，传统软件安全模型因此承受新的压力。

keypoints.title: 对 AI 安全研究方式的批评
keypoints.detail: Steinberger 批评部分学术和企业安全报告忽略推荐配置，只为制造耸动标题。他举例称，有研究者让智能体以 sudo 模式运行或关闭沙箱来强行触发漏洞，这与项目的个人智能体安全指南相违背。
keypoints.evidence: They ignored all of the recommendations we do on security... they actually fought the setup. It's actually not easy to run it in pudo mode.
keypoints.why_it_matters: 这提醒行业警惕为了关注度而歪曲智能体系统真实风险的安全研究。

keypoints.title: 通过 OpenClaw Foundation 保持独立
keypoints.detail: 为了保持中立，Steinberger 正参考 Ghost Foundation 建立 OpenClaw Foundation。该结构让项目可以接受 OpenAI、Nvidia、Microsoft 等公司的帮助，同时避免被单一企业收购或控制。
keypoints.evidence: I'm kind of building Switzerland with the open glove foundation... this will actually then help us to hire full-time people to both keep up the pace, improve the quality.
keypoints.why_it_matters: 需要兼容不同 LLM 提供商和本地模型的智能体框架，必须维持平台中立。

keypoints.title: AI 开发中的人类品味
keypoints.detail: 在代码生成日益自动化的时代，Steinberger 认为“品味”才是最终壁垒：它意味着能够识别并避开泛化、机械的 AI 味道，主动选择令人愉悦的细节与更有人格的表达。
keypoints.evidence: Taste is very important... the very low level of taste is if it doesn't stink like AI... you can identify AI written slop right away.
keypoints.why_it_matters: 当编码逐渐商品化，真正的价值会转移到产品愿景、系统设计和以人为本的最终体验。

keypoints.title: 无处不在的智能体未来
keypoints.detail: Steinberger 设想智能体能够跨设备、跨房间跟随用户，并在附近屏幕上调用项目画布。其模型是：个人拥有的“上层” OpenClaw 管理私有数据，同时与企业提供的“下层”智能体协作。
keypoints.evidence: I want to be in any room and... when you say computer I want to like talk to my agent wherever I am... it should know where I am.
keypoints.why_it_matters: 这种分层模式既保护数据隐私，也能实现企业孤立工具难以提供的高层自动化。

content.tl_dr: Peter Steinberger discusses the meteoric rise of OpenClaw as the fastest-growing open-source project and his transition to OpenAI to lead agent development while maintaining project independence through the OpenClaw Foundation.

prerequisites: Basic understanding of Large Language Models (LLMs)

content.overview: In this keynote and subsequent AMA, Peter Steinberger reflects on the first five months of OpenClaw, which he characterizes as the fastest-growing software project in GitHub history. He describes the unique challenges of 'stripper pole growth,' noting that the project has reached nearly 30,000 commits and 2,000 contributors. Steinberger addresses the intense scrutiny regarding OpenClaw's security, revealing that the project handles over 16 critical security advisories daily—double that of the Linux kernel—though he argues many represent 'AI slop' or bad-faith reports from researchers who bypass default security protocols. He emphasizes a transition toward the OpenClaw Foundation to ensure a 'Switzerland-like' neutrality, even as he works at OpenAI. The discussion explores the philosophy of 'agentic' software, where human 'taste' and system design remain the primary moats against a rising tide of AI-generated code. Steinberger ultimately advocates for a future of local data ownership and ubiquitous agents that operate with distinct personalities or 'souls.'

items.content: Project Stats: 30,000 commits, ~30,000 PRs, ~2,000 contributors within 5 months.
Security: 1,142 total advisories; 469 published; 60% closure rate. CVSS 10.0 incidents frequently reported for marginal use-cases (e.g., read/write permission bypass on unreleased features).
Dependency Risk: Supply chain attack via MS Teams/Slack through an unpinned Axios dependency.

sections.title: Project Metrics and Security Data
sections.description: Key performance indicators and security vulnerability statistics for OpenClaw.

items.content: Running a large foundation is like a company on 'hard mode' because you cannot directly command volunteers.
Agents should follow the 'Toby Luca' trust system: building reputation over time so that trusted entities get more privileged access.
Avoid 'Dark Factories' in software development; an iterative, human-led approach is superior to fully automated waterfalls because the path to the 'mountain top' is never straight.

sections.title: Managing Open Source on 'Hard Mode'
sections.description: Insights into managing high-velocity community projects and AI-driven development.

items.content: AI is fundamentally changing the security landscape by making complex multi-chain exploits easy to find, effectively 'breaking' all legacy software that hasn't accounted for agentic attackers.
The 'Soul' of an agent (its personality and quirks) is not just aesthetic but a requirement for user trust and natural interaction in non-search contexts like messaging apps.
Open source agentic frameworks act as a gateway drug for the enterprise; as individuals use them at home, they create bottom-up pressure for AI adoption in the workplace.

sections.title: Meta-Level Observations on AI Agents
sections.description: Synthesis of the current state of agentic software and industry dynamics.

keypoints.title: Hyper-growth and the 'Stripper Pole' Trajectory
keypoints.detail: OpenClaw is identified as the fastest-growing project in GitHub history, surpassing educational repos to become the largest functional software project on the platform. With 30,000 commits and nearly 30,000 PRs in five months, the velocity necessitates a shift from solo maintenance to a broad corporate coalition including Nvidia, Microsoft, and ByteDance.
keypoints.evidence: I think it's fair to say by now that we are the fastest growing project in GitHub's history... a friend called it stripper pole gross and that comes with its own challenges.
keypoints.why_it_matters: The massive scale proves a profound demand for open-source agentic frameworks that bypass corporate data silos.

keypoints.title: The Security Advisory Deluge
keypoints.detail: Steinberger reveals the project has received 1,142 security advisories, averaging 16.6 per day. He contrasts this with the Linux kernel (8-9/day) and Curl (600 total), noting that 99% are marked critical, forcing the team to contend with a new era of AI-generated vulnerability reporting.
keypoints.evidence: So far we got 1,142 advisories. That's around 16.6 a day. 99% are critical... we get like twice as much as the Linux kernel.
keypoints.why_it_matters: It highlights a new reality where AI tools can identify obscure multi-chain exploits, potentially breaking traditional software security models.

keypoints.title: Critique of AI Security Research Tactics
keypoints.detail: Steinberger criticizes certain academic and corporate security papers for ignoring recommended setups to create 'scary' headlines. He cites examples where researchers ran agents in 'sudo' mode or disabled sandboxing to force vulnerability, which contradicts the project's 'personal agent' security guidelines.
keypoints.evidence: They ignored all of the recommendations we do on security... they actually fought the setup. It's actually not easy to run it in pudo mode.
keypoints.why_it_matters: It warns against 'clout-chasing' in security research that misrepresents the true risk profile of agentic systems.

keypoints.title: Independence via the OpenClaw Foundation
keypoints.detail: To maintain neutrality, Steinberger is establishing the OpenClaw Foundation, inspired by the Ghost foundation. This structure allows the project to accept help from OpenAI, Nvidia, and Microsoft without being acquired or controlled by a single corporate entity.
keypoints.evidence: I'm kind of building Switzerland with the open glove foundation... this will actually then help us to hire full-time people to both keep up the pace, improve the quality.
keypoints.why_it_matters: Neutrality is essential for an agentic framework that must work across competing LLM providers and local models.

keypoints.title: The Role of Human 'Taste' in AI Development
keypoints.detail: In an age of automated coding, Steinberger argues that 'taste'—the ability to identify and avoid 'AI smells' or generic outputs—is the ultimate moat. He defines good taste as the deliberate choice of delightful details and human-like personality over 'AI slop.'
keypoints.evidence: Taste is very important... the very low level of taste is if it doesn't stink like AI... you can identify AI written slop right away.
keypoints.why_it_matters: As coding becomes a commodity, the value shifts to the vision and human-centric design of the final product.

keypoints.title: The Future of Ubiquitous and Agentic Systems
keypoints.detail: Steinberger envisions 'ubiquitous agents' that follow users across devices and rooms, utilizing project canvases on nearby displays. This involves a hierarchy of models where a personal 'upper-case' OpenClaw manages private data while communicating with 'lower-case' corporate agents.
keypoints.evidence: I want to be in any room and... when you say computer I want to like talk to my agent wherever I am... it should know where I am.
keypoints.why_it_matters: This model protects data privacy while enabling the high-level automation that siloed corporate tools cannot achieve.
